anchorData: PHOTO SIZES (all in cm, width × height). Full-size original print: 14 × 18 (ratio 7:9; area 252 cm²). Passport photo: 3.5 × 4.5 (ratio 7:9; area 15.75 cm²). School prize-giving poster: 70 × 90 (ratio 7:9; area 6300 cm²). Distorted trial print: 4.5 × 4.5 (ratio 1:1; area 20.25 cm²), made by keeping the height at 4.5 and stretching only the width. SCALE FACTORS: original to passport k = 3.5/14 = 4.5/18 = 1/4 (reduction). Original to poster k = 70/14 = 90/18 = 5 (enlargement). Passport to poster k = 20 (3.5×20 = 70, 4.5×20 = 90). Distorted print: width factor 4.5/14 = 9/28 (about 0.32) and height factor 1/4 (0.25), so the two factors are NOT equal. AREA FACTORS: original to passport 252 ÷ 15.75 = 16 = (1/4)⁻² i.e. the original is 16 times the passport, so passport area = (1/4)² = 1/16 of the original. Original to poster 6300 ÷ 252 = 25 = 5². Passport to poster 6300 ÷ 15.75 = 400 = 20². FACE TRIANGLE (eyes and chin: eye-gap along the top, chin distance measured down from the eye line): original eye gap 5.6, chin distance 7.2 (ratio 7:9); passport 1.4 and 1.8; poster 28 and 36; distorted print 1.8 and 1.8 (ratio 1:1). Apex angle at the chin is about 42.5° in the original, passport and poster, but about 53° in the distorted print. All corners of every print are 90°. VOLUME (Lesson 7): small carton for packing prints 10 × 6 × 4 cm = 240 cm³; large similar carton 20 × 12 × 8 cm = 1920 cm³; k = 2, volume factor 8 (240 × 8 = 1920). SHADOWS (Lesson 5): Wanjiru is 1.5 m tall and casts a 2 m shadow; at the same time a tree in the school compound casts a 12 m shadow, so tree height = 1.5/2 × 12 = 9 m (ratio 0.75). ENLARGEMENT GRID DATA: Triangle ABC with A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,2) and centre O(0,0). Lesson 8: k = 2 gives A'(2,2), B'(6,2), C'(2,4). Lesson 9: k = 1/2 gives A'(0.5,0.5), B'(1.5,0.5), C'(0.5,1); k = -2 gives A'(-2,-2), B'(-6,-2), C'(-2,-4) (inverted, on the opposite side of O). Lesson 10: object P(2,2), Q(3,2), R(2,3); image P'(4,4), Q'(7,4), R'(4,7); centre (1,1), k = 3 (check: P'-centre = (3,3) = 3 × (1,1)). MAP AND SIGN (Lesson 11): Kisumu to Nairobi straight-line distance about 265 km; on a 1:5 000 000 map this is 5.3 cm (26 500 000 cm ÷ 5 000 000). Painted sign: small sign 70 × 90 cm = 0.63 m²; enlarged sign k = 3 is 210 × 270 cm = 5.67 m² (9 × 0.63); paint costs KES 400 per m², so small sign KES 252 and large sign KES 2268 (9 × 252).
characters: Wanjiru Atieno: Grade 10 learner at Nyalenda Secondary School in Kisumu; she is the student in the photos and is 1.5 m tall. Mr Otieno: photographer at Lakeview Photo Studio, Kisumu; he prints the 3.5 × 4.5 cm passport photo and the poster. Mrs Achieng: the Mathematics teacher who poses the Driving Question Board. Prize-giving day poster: 70 × 90 cm, displayed in the school hall. Nyalenda Secondary School: has a tree that casts a 12 m shadow and a school sign painted by a local signwriter. Kisumu and Nairobi: used for the map scale example. Learners work in groups using rulers, protractors, grid paper and scissors; no electricity or internet is needed.
outcome: Wanjiru's photo keeps her likeness because the passport print (k = 1/4) and the poster (k = 5) are similar to the original: every length is multiplied by the same scale factor, so the ratios of corresponding sides stay equal (7:9 for width to height) and all corresponding angles stay equal (90° corners, about 42.5° at the chin). The distorted print multiplied the width by 9/28 and the height by 1/4, different factors, so the ratios and the chin angle (about 53°) changed and her face looked stretched. Size can change by any scale factor, but shape is kept only if one scale factor is applied to all lengths in every direction; area then changes by k² and volume by k³.
conventions: Use k for the linear scale factor, defined as k = image length ÷ object length (always state which is object and which is image). k > 1 is an enlargement; 0 < k < 1 is a reduction; negative k gives an inverted image on the opposite side of the centre. Write similar as ~ and say 'corresponding sides' and 'corresponding angles'. Always give width first then height (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm). Lengths in cm unless stated; areas in cm² or m²; volumes in cm³. Area scale factor = k²; volume scale factor = k³. 'Original' means the 14 × 18 cm print; 'image' means the resized print. Scale factor 1/4 is written as 1/4 or 0.25. Enlargement is written with centre O and scale factor k, e.g. 'enlargement, centre O(0,0), scale factor 2'. Do not use the word congruence beyond saying k = 1 gives an identical size (congruence is taught in 2.2). Say 'distorted' only for the 4.5 × 4.5 cm trial print. Use the ratio comparison 'width : height' to test similarity.

lessonMap.teaches: Launch the puzzle: size can change a lot while shape stays the same; learners record initial ideas about what must stay the same and what may change
lessonMap.usesData: Photo sizes (14 × 18, 3.5 × 4.5, 70 × 90, and distorted 4.5 × 4.5); no calculations beyond noticing

lessonMap.teaches: Identify and sort similar and non-similar figures in photos, maps, models and logos by looking at shape (visual judgement of 'same shape')
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: the idea that the passport photo and poster look like the original but the distorted print does not
lessonMap.usesData: Original, passport, poster and distorted prints as sorting cards; no numeric ratios yet

lessonMap.teaches: Similar figures have equal corresponding angles and equal ratios of corresponding sides, tested by measuring
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: sorting by shape; Lesson 1: the distorted print
lessonMap.usesData: Corner angles 90°, chin angle 42.5° vs 53°, width:height ratios 7:9 vs 1:1, face triangle measurements

lessonMap.teaches: Calculate the linear scale factor k = image ÷ object and use it to find missing lengths
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: equal ratios of corresponding sides
lessonMap.usesData: k = 1/4 (original to passport), k = 5 (original to poster), k = 20 (passport to poster), unequal factors 9/28 and 1/4 for the distorted print

lessonMap.teaches: Use similar triangles (equal angles, proportional sides) to find unknown heights with shadows
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 3 and 4: angle equality and scale factor for missing lengths
lessonMap.usesData: Wanjiru 1.5 m with 2 m shadow; tree with 12 m shadow gives 9 m

lessonMap.teaches: When lengths are multiplied by k, areas are multiplied by k²
lessonMap.usesData: Areas 252, 15.75, 6300 cm²; area factors 1/16 (passport), 25 (poster), 400 (passport to poster)

lessonMap.teaches: When lengths are multiplied by k, volumes are multiplied by k³
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: k; Lesson 6: k² pattern for area
lessonMap.usesData: Cartons 10 × 6 × 4 = 240 cm³ and 20 × 12 × 8 = 1920 cm³, k = 2, volume factor 8

lessonMap.focus: Enlargement with a centre and positive scale factor
lessonMap.teaches: Construct an enlargement from a centre of enlargement using rays and a positive scale factor greater than 1
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 4 and 3: scale factor and similarity of object and image
lessonMap.usesData: Triangle ABC A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,2), centre O(0,0), k = 2 giving A'(2,2), B'(6,2), C'(2,4)

lessonMap.teaches: Enlargements with 0 < k < 1 give reductions and negative k gives an inverted image on the opposite side of the centre
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 8: construction with rays from the centre
lessonMap.usesData: Triangle ABC with centre O(0,0): k = 1/2 and k = -2 images; link k = 1/4 passport reduction and projector inversion

lessonMap.focus: Finding the centre and scale factor
lessonMap.teaches: Find the centre of enlargement by joining corresponding points of object and image, and find k from the lengths
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 8 and 9: how images are constructed from a centre and k

lessonMap.focus: Applications of scale and area/volume factors
lessonMap.teaches: Apply scale factors, area factors and volume factors to scale drawings, maps, models and costing of painted signs
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 4, 6 and 7: k, k² and k³
lessonMap.usesData: Map scale 1:5 000 000 with Kisumu to Nairobi 265 km = 5.3 cm; sign 0.63 m² to 5.67 m² at KES 400 per m² (KES 252 and KES 2268)

lessonMap.focus: Consolidation and resolving the Driving Question
lessonMap.teaches: Synthesise ratios, angles and scale factors into one complete explanation of why the passport photo is not distorted while the 4.5 × 4.5 print is
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1 to 11, especially 3 (ratios and angles), 4 (k) and 6 (k²)
lessonMap.usesData: All photo sizes, face triangle, 42.5° vs 53°, factors 1/4, 5, 20, 9/28, area factors 16, 25, 400
